title: Parallelizing section summaries

goals.goal: Verify with a real run and compare timings

delivered: Threaded section + polish stages in transcript-reader, with a lock around the shared session file and a README note.
checked: Full pipeline on a cloned session (27.8s, 8 sections, 100% coverage) and a cold/warm resume run. Never killed a worker mid-burst.
headline: The probe did its job: the concurrency limit was retired before any code changed, and the thread pool plus a lock landed without drama. The measurement that justifies the worker count came four minutes after the constant was written, and the one real defect surfaced only because the actual pipeline was run on a clone instead of trusting the unit benchmark.

phases.name: Retire the unknown
phases.why: the provider's concurrency limit was unknown and decides the whole design; 30 seconds of probing buys the right to commit

nodes.claim: 7 concurrent requests succeed — 2.1s wall versus ~14s serial-equivalent

phases.name: Design the change
phases.why: sections are independent I/O, but progress writes share one read-modify-write file, so the lock has to land before the pool does
phases.quote: That *will* race if called from worker threads.

nodes.claim: Each section is one HTTP call with no shared state — safe to parallelize
nodes.evidence: code read of the section loop

nodes.claim: update_meta is a read-modify-write on session.json — a real race once workers call it
nodes.evidence: code read, then a module lock added at 07:55:05
written at 07:55:37; the token measurement that tests it ran at 07:57:49 — after

gate.question: How many workers should run at once?

options.text: 6, one below what the probe held
options.why: the probe used tiny requests; real ones are 2200 tokens each, so 6 caps the burst
the probe showed 7 was fine, and 4 leaves most of the win unclaimed
never exercised above 7, and it multiplies the token burst further

nodes.claim: The burst is 10.2k peak input tokens — comfortable for this provider

phases.name: Prove it on real data
phases.why: a faster loop only counts if the output quality holds, so the benchmark measures points per section as well as wall clock

nodes.claim: Same transcript: 76.9s sequential versus 20.5s at 6 workers
One section produced 2 points instead of 3 — five sequential runs gave 3,3,3,3,2, so it is sampling variance, not the change

phases.name: Break it
phases.why: a green unit benchmark says nothing about the wiring, so the real entry point runs on a cloned session
phases.quote: rather than trusting the unit benchmark

nodes.claim: The parallelized pipeline works end to end
The worker returns (index, generated); the merge was handed the whole tuple

phases.name: Close it
phases.why: checkpoints are what make a killed run cheap, so the warm path has to be shown to still reuse them

nodes.claim: Cold run 32.0s, warm run 0.1s — checkpoints are reused
An unfamiliar session with a real document was left alone; only the agent's own probe dirs were deleted
nodes.evidence: judgment call; its creation timestamp falls inside this session, so provenance is not provable from the log

nodes.claim: A worker killed mid-burst leaves the other six checkpoints intact
nodes.evidence: never tested — only cold and warm runs were tried

lessons.text: Measure before committing to a number that shows up in the diff. The worker constant was written at 07:55:37; the measurement that justified it ran at 07:57:49. It happened to agree, which is exactly why the ordering is worth remembering.
A unit-level benchmark does not prove the integration. The only defect in the change was invisible until the real pipeline ran on a clone.
lessons.node: The parallelized pipeline works end to end

lessons.text: Before calling an intermittent result a regression, re-run the thing that varied. Five sequential runs answering 3,3,3,3,2 turned a suspected defect into a property of the model.
lessons.node: One section produced 2 points instead of 3

lessons.text: Probe the limit before designing to it. The 30-second concurrency test is the reason the pool landed at 6 with no 429s and no backtracking.

open: No failure-path test: nobody killed a worker mid-burst to prove the surviving checkpoints still resume. The resume test only covers the clean-interruption case.
The run emitted 1 warning — 'section 6 point 2 spans 00:04:36-00:05:54, outside section 00:03:50-00:05:16' — observed at 08:06:40 and never explained.
